content.text: Closed form written for this catalogue: f′(x) = a·x, so x_{n+1} = x_n − η·f′(x_n) = (1 − η·a)·x_n and, by induction, x_n = x0·(1 − η·a)^n. For x0 ≠ 0 the positions tend to 0 exactly when |1 − η·a| < 1, that is 0 < η·a < 2. Not independently reviewed.

The objective is exactly the quadratic f(x) = a·x²/2 with a > 0: no noise and no higher-order terms. The step size η is the same for every update. Evaluation is deterministic on every conforming JavaScript engine: values come from exactly specified arithmetic rounded once (a logarithm only estimates the first index of a numerical limit, which is then verified exactly), so the same parameters and iteration always give the same values. Real numbers are IEEE-754 double-precision values; the product η·a is computed once in double precision and the regime is classified from it.

content.text: Derivation written for this catalogue: expanding A·(x + h)² + B·(x + h) + C gives (f(x + h) − f(x))/h = 2A·x + B + A·h for every h ≠ 0, so the secant slope differs from f′(x) = 2A·x + B by exactly A·h and tends to it as h → 0; at h = 0 the quotient is 0/0. When A ≠ 0, f′(x) = 0 only at x = −B/(2A). Not independently reviewed.

The function is exactly the quadratic f(x) = A·x² + B·x + C with real coefficients; A = 0 gives a straight line and A = B = 0 a constant. The derivative is the analytical derivative f′(x) = 2A·x + B of this polynomial. It is not estimated from secant slopes, samples or a numerical limit. Inputs are IEEE-754 double-precision values taken at their exact values; the second point is evaluated at the exact sum p + h. Evaluation is deterministic on every conforming JavaScript engine: only exactly specified arithmetic is used, so the same parameters always give the same values.

assumptions: The function is exactly the quadratic f(x) = A·x² + B·x + C with real coefficients; A = 0 gives a straight line and A = B = 0 a constant.
The derivative is the analytical derivative f′(x) = 2A·x + B of this polynomial. It is not estimated from secant slopes, samples or a numerical limit.
Inputs are IEEE-754 double-precision values taken at their exact values; the second point is evaluated at the exact sum p + h.
Evaluation is deterministic on every conforming JavaScript engine: only exactly specified arithmetic is used, so the same parameters always give the same values.
limitations: Each quantity is its exact value rounded to the nearest double once. Categories come from exact signs, so a slope that displays as 0 can still be classified as increasing or decreasing.
A probe entered as a decimal is in general not exactly at a vertex whose position is not a binary fraction (for example −1/3), so the slope there is a small nonzero number.
The secant slope is undefined at h = 0 and no limiting value is substituted. For h ≠ 0 it differs from the derivative by exactly A·h.
The domain constraint −5 ≤ p + h ≤ 5 is evaluated on the double sum p + h, as by every runtime entry point; the exact sum can then lie outside by at most 2^−51, and Q is evaluated at that exact sum.

Values outside the double range are statuses: a nonzero value that rounds to zero is a numerical limit (UNDERFLOW), subnormal values carry a reduced-precision note, and the vertex of a curve with a tiny nonzero A can exceed the largest double (OVERFLOW).

The graphs of f and f′ are sampled at 401 positions from −5 to 5 in double precision; the polyline between samples does not certify values between them. Tangent and secant lines are drawn from correctly rounded endpoints, and an endpoint whose exact value is nonzero but below the double range is drawn at 0.

sources.citation: Derivation written for this catalogue: expanding A·(x + h)² + B·(x + h) + C gives (f(x + h) − f(x))/h = 2A·x + B + A·h for every h ≠ 0, so the secant slope differs from f′(x) = 2A·x + B by exactly A·h and tends to it as h → 0; at h = 0 the quotient is 0/0. When A ≠ 0, f′(x) = 0 only at x = −B/(2A). Not independently reviewed.

content.text: Derivation written for this catalogue: for v = vx·e₁ + vy·e₂, linearity gives M·v = vx·(M·e₁) + vy·(M·e₂), so the columns of M are the images of e₁ and e₂ and fix the whole map. The image of the unit square is the parallelogram spanned by the columns, with signed area det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21; |det M| scales every area and the sign of det M records whether the counterclockwise order of e₁, e₂ is kept. Eigenvalues are the roots of λ² − (tr M)·λ + det M = 0, real exactly when Δ = (tr M)² − 4·det M ≥ 0; when Δ = 0 and M ≠ λ·I the matrix M − λI has rank 1 and a single eigen-direction. Not independently reviewed.

M is a real 2×2 matrix acting linearly on the plane; every statement is about the matrix with exactly the stored entries. Entries and test-vector components are IEEE-754 double-precision values in [−3, 3]; every value of that range, including 0 and the zero vector, is an allowed experiment. Orientation, rank and the unchanged-direction category are decided from exact signs and exact equalities for the stored entries, never from a tolerance or from rounded display digits. Evaluation is deterministic on every conforming JavaScript engine: exact integer arithmetic, IEEE-754 rounding and one correctly rounded square root per unit direction, so the same entries and test vector always give the same values.

Study Harness visualizer implementation report §12.2: 2×2 matrix with an explicit column-vector convention, basis vectors, test vector, transformed grid, determinant and nonnegative area when authorized, prediction of orientation, collapse and unchanged directions, and the identity, nonaxis rotation, nonsymmetric shear, reflection, singular collapse, zero matrix and zero vector reference cases.
Each example sets all four matrix entries and the test vector. Rotation entries are the nearest stored values of cos and sin.

manifest.title: A 2×2 matrix as a transformation of the plane
manifest.summary: A real 2×2 matrix M with entries in [−3, 3] acting on column vectors: images of the basis vectors (the columns of M), of a test vector, of a reference grid and of the unit square; the determinant, the nonnegative area scale, orientation, rank and the real eigen-directions where they exist.

m11.description: Entry m11 of M (row 1, column 1). Column 1 of M is the image M·e1 of the basis vector e1.

m12.description: Entry m12 of M (row 1, column 2). Column 2 of M is the image M·e2 of the basis vector e2.

m21.description: Entry m21 of M (row 2, column 1). Column 1 of M is the image M·e1 of the basis vector e1.

m22.label: Matrix entry row 2, column 2
m22.description: Entry m22 of M (row 2, column 2). Column 2 of M is the image M·e2 of the basis vector e2.

vx.label: Test vector x component
vx.description: The x component of the test vector v before the transformation. The zero vector is allowed.

vy.label: Test vector y component
vy.description: The y component of the test vector v before the transformation. The zero vector is allowed.

basis.e1.label: Basis vector e₁
basis.e1.meaning: The standard basis vector e₁ = (1, 0) before the transformation; a fixed reference.
basis.e1.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
basis.e1.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up.

basis.e2.label: Basis vector e₂
basis.e2.meaning: The standard basis vector e₂ = (0, 1) before the transformation; a fixed reference.
basis.e2.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
basis.e2.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up.

vector.v.label: Test vector v
vector.v.meaning: The test vector v = (vx, vy) before the transformation, equal to the stored parameters. It may be the zero vector.
vector.v.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
vector.v.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up.

image.e1.label: Image of e₁
image.e1.meaning: M·e₁ = (m11, m21): the FIRST COLUMN of M (column-vector convention), the point where e₁ lands.
image.e1.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
image.e1.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up.

image.e2.label: Image of e₂
image.e2.meaning: M·e₂ = (m12, m22): the second column of M, the point where e₂ lands.
image.e2.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
image.e2.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up.

image.v.label: Image of v
image.v.meaning: M·v = (m11·vx + m12·vy, m21·vx + m22·vy) = vx·(M·e₁) + vy·(M·e₂), exact and rounded once. It is the zero vector when v = 0 or when v lies along a collapsed direction; the zero vector is a valid result, not an undefined one.
image.v.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
image.v.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up.

determinant.label: Determinant
determinant.meaning: det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21 for the stored entries, exact and rounded once: the signed factor by which M scales areas.
determinant.signConvention: Positive when M keeps the counterclockwise order of e₁ then e₂, negative when it reverses that order, zero when the plane collapses onto a line or a point.

area.scale.label: Area scale
area.scale.meaning: The nonnegative factor |det M| by which M multiplies every area: the area of the image of the unit square. A negative determinant reverses orientation; it never makes an area negative.

orientation.label: Orientation
orientation.meaning: From the exact sign of det M for the stored entries: preserved (det M > 0, the counterclockwise order of e₁ then e₂ is kept), reversed (det M < 0, the order is flipped as by a reflection), collapsed (det M = 0, the plane is flattened onto a line or a point). Never from rounded digits.
orientation.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
orientation.signConvention: Counterclockwise (from +x toward +y) is the positive orientation of the plane.

rank.label: Rank
rank.meaning: Dimension of the image of M, decided exactly for the stored entries: 2 when det M ≠ 0, 1 when det M = 0 and M is not the zero matrix (the plane collapses onto a line), 0 for the zero matrix (every vector maps to the origin).

image.direction.label: Collapse line direction
image.direction.meaning: For rank 1 only: the unit direction of the line through the origin onto which M collapses the plane (the line spanned by the columns of M). Undefined with FULL_RANK for rank 2 (the image is the whole plane) and with ZERO_IMAGE for the zero matrix (the image is a single point).
image.direction.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
image.direction.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up. A line through the origin has two unit directions; the one whose first nonzero component is positive is reported.

trace.label: Trace
trace.meaning: tr M = m11 + m22, exact and rounded once: the sum of the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity, complex ones included).

eigen.discriminant.label: Eigenvalue discriminant
eigen.discriminant.meaning: Δ = (tr M)² − 4·det M = (m11 − m22)² + 4·m12·m21 for the stored entries, exact and rounded once. Δ > 0: two distinct real eigenvalues; Δ = 0: one repeated eigenvalue; Δ < 0: a complex-conjugate pair. Its exact sign decides the eigen category.

eigen.category.label: Unchanged-direction category
eigen.category.meaning: How many directions through the origin M maps onto their own line (M·u = λ·u, with λ possibly negative or zero), decided exactly: two-real (Δ > 0: exactly two such directions), repeated-scalar (M = λ·I: every direction), repeated-defective (Δ = 0 and M ≠ λ·I: exactly one direction), complex (Δ < 0: no real direction). A real matrix does not always have two visible real eigenvectors.

eigen.values.label: Real eigenvalues
eigen.values.meaning: The real eigenvalues (λ₁, λ₂) with λ₁ ≥ λ₂, roots of λ² − (tr M)·λ + det M = 0 listed with multiplicity (a repeated eigenvalue appears twice). Undefined with COMPLEX_EIGENVALUES when Δ < 0. Irrational values agree with the exact roots to within a few units in the last place.
eigen.values.signConvention: A negative eigenvalue reverses vectors along its direction; zero sends that direction to the origin.

eigen.direction1.label: First eigen-direction
eigen.direction1.meaning: A unit vector u₁ with M·u₁ = λ₁·u₁: for two distinct real eigenvalues the direction of λ₁, and for a repeated eigenvalue with M ≠ λ·I the single unchanged direction. Undefined with COMPLEX_EIGENVALUES (no real direction is unchanged) or ALL_DIRECTIONS (M = λ·I: every direction is unchanged, so none is singled out).
eigen.direction1.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
eigen.direction1.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up. A line through the origin has two unit directions; the one whose first nonzero component is positive is reported.

eigen.direction2.label: Second eigen-direction
eigen.direction2.meaning: A unit vector u₂ with M·u₂ = λ₂·u₂ for two distinct real eigenvalues. Undefined with SINGLE_DIRECTION (a repeated eigenvalue with only one unchanged direction), COMPLEX_EIGENVALUES or ALL_DIRECTIONS.
eigen.direction2.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
eigen.direction2.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up. A line through the origin has two unit directions; the one whose first nonzero component is positive is reported.

grid.original.label: Reference grid
grid.original.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
grid.original.description: The 14 segments x = k from (k, −3) to (k, 3) and y = k from (−3, k) to (3, k) for the integers k = −3…3, before the transformation.

grid.transformed.label: Transformed grid
grid.transformed.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
grid.transformed.description: The image of each reference-grid segment: a linear map sends a segment to the segment between the images of its endpoints, so x = k maps to the segment from M·(k, −3) to M·(k, 3), and likewise for y = k. Endpoints are exact and rounded once. When M collapses the plane the images lie on one line (rank 1) or at the origin (rank 0), and a segment can have equal endpoints.

unit-square.label: Unit square
unit-square.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
unit-square.description: The unit square with vertices (0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (0, 1) in counterclockwise order, before the transformation.

unit-square.image.label: Image of the unit square
unit-square.image.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
unit-square.image.description: The parallelogram with vertices 0, M·e₁, M·e₁ + M·e₂ and M·e₂, in that order. Its area is |det M|; the vertex order is counterclockwise when det M > 0 and clockwise when det M < 0. `degenerate` is true exactly when det M = 0, when the parallelogram is a segment or a point.

eigen.lines.label: Unchanged-direction lines
eigen.lines.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
eigen.lines.description: For each reported unit eigen-direction u, the segment from −9·u to 9·u on the line through the origin that M maps into itself (IDs u1, u2 follow the eigen-direction quantities). No segment when the eigenvalues are complex (no real direction) or when M = λ·I (every direction); the eigen-direction quantities state which.

interpretation.coordinateConvention: Column-vector convention: vectors are columns and M acts by M·v. M·e₁ = (m11, m21) is the FIRST COLUMN of M and M·e₂ = (m12, m22) is the second column; entry m_ij is in row i, column j. The plane has x to the right and y up; counterclockwise from +x toward +y is the positive orientation.
assumptions: M is a real 2×2 matrix acting linearly on the plane; every statement is about the matrix with exactly the stored entries.
Entries and test-vector components are IEEE-754 double-precision values in [−3, 3]; every value of that range, including 0 and the zero vector, is an allowed experiment.
Orientation, rank and the unchanged-direction category are decided from exact signs and exact equalities for the stored entries, never from a tolerance or from rounded display digits.

Evaluation is deterministic on every conforming JavaScript engine: exact integer arithmetic, IEEE-754 rounding and one correctly rounded square root per unit direction, so the same entries and test vector always give the same values.
limitations: A decimal entry such as 0.7 is stored as the nearest double. A matrix that is singular in decimal arithmetic, such as columns (0.1, 0.3) and (0.7, 2.1), can be invertible as stored, with a determinant near 4e-17; the classification follows the stored values and the determinant shows it. Display rounding is separate from computation.
Rotations by angles other than multiples of 90° have irrational entries; their stored entries are the nearest doubles, so for example det M differs from 1 by about 1e-16.

Rational quantities (images, M·v, determinant, area scale, trace, discriminant, grid and square vertices) are exact and rounded once. Irrational quantities (eigenvalues from a non-square discriminant, unit directions) agree with the exact values to within a few units in the last place.
A nonzero value too small to represent is a numerical-limit (UNDERFLOW) status, never zero; computed subnormal values carry an UNDERFLOW approximation note.
The grid covers only the integer lines −3 ≤ k ≤ 3, and unchanged-direction lines are drawn with half-length 9; both are bounded drawings of unbounded lines.
Only real eigen-directions are drawn. Complex eigenvalues are reported as a status; their rotation-like behaviour is not decomposed.

content.text: Derivation written for this catalogue: u·v = Σ u_i v_i = |u||v| cos θ; u×v = (u_y v_z − u_z v_y, u_z v_x − u_x v_z, u_x v_y − u_y v_x) with e_x × e_y = e_z in a right-handed frame, so |u×v| = |u||v| sin θ and |u×v|² + (u·v)² = |u|²|v|² (Lagrange's identity). Hence θ = atan2(|u×v|, u·v) ∈ [0, π], defined when u ≠ 0 and v ≠ 0; u×v = 0 exactly when a vector is zero or u and v are parallel or antiparallel, and then it has no direction. Not independently reviewed.

u and v are dimensionless vectors in a right-handed Cartesian frame; their components are exact IEEE-754 double values. The cross product follows the right-hand rule: e_x × e_y = e_z, e_y × e_z = e_x, e_z × e_x = e_y. Two nonzero vectors are classified with the tolerance τ = 1/10¹²: parallel or antiparallel when sin θ ≤ τ, orthogonal when |cos θ| ≤ τ, decided exactly from the inputs. Evaluation is deterministic within one JavaScript engine: θ, the unit directions and the angle arc use Math.atan2, Math.cos, Math.sin and exponentiation, which ECMAScript lets each engine approximate, so their last bits can differ between engines; the dot and cross products, the lengths and the relationship are computed exactly and are the same on every engine.

Study Harness visualizer implementation report §12.4 (spatial vector orientation: two vectors, their angle, dot and cross products with declared handedness, coordinate projections, orientation presets, exact numeric alternatives, parallel, antiparallel, orthogonal and zero-vector checks) and §11 (3D equivalents).
Preset pairs of vectors, named by their components, for comparing different orientations.

interpretation.coordinateConvention: Right-handed Cartesian frame with axes x, y, z and e_x × e_y = e_z; u and v are free vectors drawn from the common origin. The xy projection is viewed from +z, the xz projection from −y and the yz projection from +x, each with its first named axis to the right and the second up.
interpretation.angleConvention: θ is the unsigned angle between u and v in radians, 0 ≤ θ ≤ π, computed as atan2(|u×v|, u·v). Degree display converts at the presentation boundary (1° = π/180 rad); the canonical value stays in radians.
assumptions: u and v are dimensionless vectors in a right-handed Cartesian frame; their components are exact IEEE-754 double values.
The cross product follows the right-hand rule: e_x × e_y = e_z, e_y × e_z = e_x, e_z × e_x = e_y.
Two nonzero vectors are classified with the tolerance τ = 1/10¹²: parallel or antiparallel when sin θ ≤ τ, orthogonal when |cos θ| ≤ τ, decided exactly from the inputs.

Evaluation is deterministic within one JavaScript engine: θ, the unit directions and the angle arc use Math.atan2, Math.cos, Math.sin and exponentiation, which ECMAScript lets each engine approximate, so their last bits can differ between engines; the dot and cross products, the lengths and the relationship are computed exactly and are the same on every engine.
limitations: Dot products, cross-product components and lengths are rounded once from exact values; θ and the unit direction are computed from those rounded, rescaled values and agree with exact references to a few units in the last place.

The classification is a tolerance decision on exact values, not a property of displayed digits: decimal inputs that are not exactly proportional in binary can be parallel within the tolerance while u×v is a tiny nonzero vector with a defined, input-sensitive direction.

A nonzero result smaller than the smallest representable number is a numerical-limit status, never 0; an inexact result below the smallest normal double is reported as a reduced-precision approximation.

The cross product is drawn at true scale and can leave the default view; the unit direction is drawn with length 1. The angle arc is sampled at 33 points; the polyline between samples is a drawing aid.
Projections onto coordinate planes drop one component each, so a single projection cannot show whether two vectors are parallel or orthogonal in space.

content.text: Derivation written for this catalogue: f(x, y) = ½·[x y]·H·[x y]ᵀ with H = [[a, b], [b, c]], so ∇f = H·[x y]ᵀ = (a·x + b·y, b·x + c·y). H is positive definite exactly when a > 0 and a·c − b² > 0; then f(x, y) > 0 for (x, y) ≠ (0, 0), the origin is the unique minimum with f = 0, and ∇f = 0 only there because H is invertible. On the ray (x, y) = r·(cos t, sin t), f = r²·q(t)/2 with q(t) = a·cos²t + 2b·cos t·sin t + c·sin²t > 0, so the level f = L is the closed ellipse r(t) = √(2L/q(t)). f is constant along a level curve, so ∇f is perpendicular to its tangent. The axis sections are f(x, 0) = a·x²/2 and f(0, y) = c·y²/2. Not independently reviewed.

f is exactly the quadratic form (a·x² + 2b·x·y + c·y²)/2 with constant coefficients: no noise and no higher-order terms. The Hessian H = [[a, b], [b, c]] is symmetric positive definite: a ≥ 0.2, c ≥ 0.2 and a·c − b² > 0 (constraint positive-definite). Degenerate troughs (a·c − b² = 0) and saddles (a·c − b² < 0) are outside this model. The gradient is the vector of partial derivatives (∂f/∂x, ∂f/∂y) = (a·x + b·y, b·x + c·y); it points toward increasing f. Coefficients and coordinates are dimensionless IEEE-754 double values; evaluation is deterministic within one JavaScript engine. The 3D view and its camera are presentation only: the kernel has no camera input, and turning or resetting the view never changes a, b, c or the point.

Each comparison setting fixes a, b, c and the point p.

manifest.title: Gradient on a positive-definite quadratic surface
manifest.summary: The surface f(x, y) = (a·x² + 2b·x·y + c·y²)/2 with a·c − b² > 0 and a selected point p in [−2, 2]²: f(p), the gradient ∇f(p) with its length and direction (undefined at the minimum), the Hessian determinant, the minimum, a sampled surface, analytic contour ellipses, a gradient field with disclosed arrow scale and the two axis cross-sections, all from one static evaluation.

a.label: Coefficient a
a.description: Coefficient of x²/2: the curvature of f along the x-axis (∂²f/∂x²). Must be positive.

b.label: Coefficient b
b.description: Coupling coefficient of x·y (∂²f/∂x∂y). Nonzero values tilt the contour ellipses away from the axes; together with a and c it must keep a·c − b² > 0.

c.label: Coefficient c
c.description: Coefficient of y²/2: the curvature of f along the y-axis (∂²f/∂y²). Must be positive.

px.label: Point x-coordinate
px.description: The x-coordinate of the selected point p. Any value from −2 to 2 is allowed, including 0.

py.label: Point y-coordinate
py.description: The y-coordinate of the selected point p. Any value from −2 to 2 is allowed, including 0.

point.label: Selected point
point.meaning: The selected point p = (p_x, p_y), equal to its two parameters.
point.coordinateFrame: xy plane of a right-handed frame: x to the right, y up when viewed from +z
point.signConvention: Components along +x (right) and +y (up) in the xy plane.

value.label: Height at the point
value.meaning: f(p) = (a·p_x² + 2b·p_x·p_y + c·p_y²)/2, the exact value rounded once. Positive except at the minimum.
value.coordinateFrame: graph space of a right-handed frame: x and y horizontal, z = f(x, y) up
value.signConvention: Height above the xy plane along +z; never negative on this family.

gradient.label: Gradient at the point
gradient.meaning: Vector of partial derivatives ∇f(p) = (∂f/∂x, ∂f/∂y) = (a·p_x + b·p_y, b·p_x + c·p_y), each component rounded once. It is the zero vector only at the minimum.
gradient.coordinateFrame: xy plane of a right-handed frame: x to the right, y up when viewed from +z
gradient.signConvention: Points toward increasing f (uphill); components along +x (right) and +y (up).

gradient.norm.label: Length of the gradient
gradient.norm.meaning: |∇f(p)| = √((∂f/∂x)² + (∂f/∂y)²): the rate of increase of f per unit distance in the direction of the gradient.
gradient.norm.coordinateFrame: xy plane of a right-handed frame: x to the right, y up when viewed from +z
gradient.norm.signConvention: A length: never negative; 0 only at the minimum.

gradient.direction.label: Direction of the gradient
gradient.direction.meaning: Unit vector ∇f(p)/|∇f(p)|, the direction of fastest increase of f. Undefined (ZERO_GRADIENT) at the minimum p = (0, 0), where the gradient is zero; no direction is ever chosen in its place. Decided from p itself, so a tiny nonzero point keeps a defined direction.
gradient.direction.coordinateFrame: xy plane of a right-handed frame: x to the right, y up when viewed from +z
gradient.direction.signConvention: Unit vector toward increasing f; components along +x (right) and +y (up).

hessian.det.label: Hessian determinant
hessian.det.meaning: Determinant a·c − b² of the constant Hessian H = [[a, b], [b, c]], rounded once. Positive on the whole admissible domain (constraint positive-definite).
hessian.det.signConvention: Positive for every admissible coefficient set.

minimum.location.label: Location of the minimum
minimum.location.meaning: The unique minimum of the symmetric positive-definite family: (0, 0) for every admissible a, b and c, because H is positive definite and ∇f = 0 only at the origin.
minimum.location.coordinateFrame: xy plane of a right-handed frame: x to the right, y up when viewed from +z
minimum.location.signConvention: Components along +x (right) and +y (up) in the xy plane.

minimum.value.label: Minimum value
minimum.value.meaning: f(0, 0) = 0, the unique lowest value of f on this family.
minimum.value.coordinateFrame: graph space of a right-handed frame: x and y horizontal, z = f(x, y) up
minimum.value.signConvention: Height along +z; f is never below it.

arrow.scale.label: Arrow length scale
arrow.scale.meaning: Factor s by which drawn gradient arrows are shortened or lengthened: each arrow is drawn as s·∇f. s is chosen per frame from 1, 0.5, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05, 0.02, … as the largest value with s·M ≤ 0.45, where M is the longest gradient on the 9 × 9 field grid (90% of its spacing 0.5). Presentation scale only: no quantity is changed by it.
arrow.scale.signConvention: Positive; 1 means arrows are drawn at true length.

surface.label: Surface samples
surface.description: f(x, y) sampled on a 41 × 41 grid x, y = −2, −1.9, …, 2 (spacing 0.1), z stored row by row in y. The mesh between samples is a drawing aid; it does not certify values between them.
surface.coordinateFrame: graph space of a right-handed frame: x and y horizontal, z = f(x, y) up

contours.label: Contour lines
contours.description: One closed ellipse f(x, y) = L for each level L = 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, in that order, computed analytically as r(t) = √(2L/q(t)) with q(t) = a·cos²t + 2b·cos t·sin t + c·sin²t at the 180 directions t = 2πk/180 counterclockwise from +x, with the first point repeated to close the curve (181 points per level; a closed curve has no endpoints). Large levels and elongated ellipses can extend beyond the default view.
contours.coordinateFrame: xy plane of a right-handed frame: x to the right, y up when viewed from +z

field.label: Gradient field
field.description: The gradient ∇f at the 9 × 9 grid points x, y = −2, −1.5, …, 2 (spacing 0.5), row by row in y. Vectors are true values; they are drawn at s·∇f with the disclosed scale s (see arrow.scale). The zero vector at the origin has no direction and is drawn as a dot.
field.coordinateFrame: xy plane of a right-handed frame: x to the right, y up when viewed from +z

cross-section-x.label: Cross-section along the x-axis
cross-section-x.description: The section f(x, 0) = a·x²/2 sampled at 81 points x = −2, −1.95, …, 2 (spacing 0.05); the polyline between samples is a drawing aid.
cross-section-x.coordinateFrame: vertical section y = 0: horizontal x to the right, vertical z = f(x, 0) up

cross-section-y.label: Cross-section along the y-axis
cross-section-y.description: The section f(0, y) = c·y²/2 sampled at 81 points y = −2, −1.95, …, 2 (spacing 0.05); the polyline between samples is a drawing aid.
cross-section-y.coordinateFrame: vertical section x = 0: horizontal y to the right, vertical z = f(0, y) up

point-2d.label: Selected point in the contour view
point-2d.coordinateFrame: xy plane of a right-handed frame: x to the right, y up when viewed from +z

point-3d.label: Selected point on the surface
point-3d.description: The point (p_x, p_y, f(p)) on the surface (ID "p"), or a gap with a reason when f(p) is a numerical limit.
point-3d.coordinateFrame: graph space of a right-handed frame: x and y horizontal, z = f(x, y) up

gradient-2d.label: Gradient arrow in the contour view
gradient-2d.description: Segment (ID "gradient") from p to p + s·∇f(p), drawn at length s·|∇f(p)| with the arrow scale s (quantity arrow.scale), the same scale as the gradient field; its direction is exact. Empty at the minimum, where the gradient is zero, and when the scaled arrow is too short to have distinct endpoints.
gradient-2d.coordinateFrame: xy plane of a right-handed frame: x to the right, y up when viewed from +z

gradient-3d.label: Gradient arrow on the surface
gradient-3d.description: Segment (ID "gradient") from (p, f(p)) to (p + s·∇f(p), f(p)) in the horizontal plane z = f(p), drawn at length s·|∇f(p)| with the arrow scale s (quantity arrow.scale), the same scale as the gradient field; its direction is exact. Empty at the minimum, when the scaled arrow has no extent, or when f(p) is a numerical limit.
gradient-3d.coordinateFrame: graph space of a right-handed frame: x and y horizontal, z = f(x, y) up

constraints.message: The coefficients must satisfy a·c − b² > 0. Only then is the surface a bowl with a single lowest point, which is the family this activity covers; at a·c − b² = 0 the surface becomes a trough with a whole line of lowest points, and below 0 a saddle.
constraints.recovery: Reduce the size of b (move b toward 0), or increase a or c, until a·c − b² is greater than 0.

interpretation.coordinateConvention: Right-handed Cartesian frame with x to the right and y up in the contour view (viewed from +z) and z = f(x, y) up in the 3D view. Contour, field, point and arrow coordinates share the xy plane; the cross-sections are the vertical planes y = 0 (horizontal axis x) and x = 0 (horizontal axis y).
interpretation.angleConvention: Contour sample directions t are in radians, measured counterclockwise from +x toward +y.
assumptions: f is exactly the quadratic form (a·x² + 2b·x·y + c·y²)/2 with constant coefficients: no noise and no higher-order terms.

The Hessian H = [[a, b], [b, c]] is symmetric positive definite: a ≥ 0.2, c ≥ 0.2 and a·c − b² > 0 (constraint positive-definite). Degenerate troughs (a·c − b² = 0) and saddles (a·c − b² < 0) are outside this model.
The gradient is the vector of partial derivatives (∂f/∂x, ∂f/∂y) = (a·x + b·y, b·x + c·y); it points toward increasing f.
Coefficients and coordinates are dimensionless IEEE-754 double values; evaluation is deterministic within one JavaScript engine.
The 3D view and its camera are presentation only: the kernel has no camera input, and turning or resetting the view never changes a, b, c or the point.
limitations: Point values — f(p), ∇f(p), |∇f(p)|, the direction ∇f/|∇f| and a·c − b² — are computed exactly from the double inputs (exact binary arithmetic, with integer square roots for the length and the direction) and each is rounded once to the nearest double, ties to even. Sampled surface heights, section heights and field vectors use about 106-bit intermediates and agree with the exactly rounded values to a unit in the last place.

Results below the smallest normal double are reduced-precision approximations; a nonzero f(p) or gradient length that rounds to 0 is a numerical-limit status, never 0, a nonzero gradient or direction component shown as 0 carries an approximation note, and the gradient direction stays defined at every point other than the origin.
The surface is sampled on a 41 × 41 grid with spacing 0.1 and the cross-sections at 81 points each; the drawing between samples does not certify values between them.

Contours are exact ellipses sampled at 180 directions per level for L = 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 only. Because the coordinates are rounded, f at a contour point equals L to about 4·√(λmax/λmin)·2⁻⁵³ relative (better than 10⁻¹² unless λmax/λmin exceeds about 10⁶). Directions use the platform Math.cos and Math.sin, so the last bits of sample positions can differ between JavaScript engines; f = L at each point holds regardless.

Gradient arrows (the point's arrow and the 9 × 9 field) are drawn at s·∇f with the disclosed scale s ≤ 1 chosen per frame; the arrow at p can therefore not be compared in length across frames without the scale.
Only the axis cross-sections f(x, 0) and f(0, y) are provided; sections along other lines are not part of this model.
